last.verdict: Opendoor's inventory ballooned while margins shrank, and guidance points to a much bigger fourth-quarter loss in a weak housing market.

takeaways.label: Bigger loss ahead
takeaways.text: Opendoor guides to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70M–$85M in Q4, versus $31M in Q3, and says profit on homes sold will fall again.

takeaways.label: Thinner margins
takeaways.text: Profit after direct costs fell to 3.3% of revenue from 5.8% last quarter. Gross margin dropped to 3.7% from 9.7%, and profit per home sold fell to $12K from $22K.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt build
takeaways.text: Homes held rose to 7,596 from 5,459, worth $2.6B. Operating cash outflow was $1.8B in nine months, funded by $1.8B of new property-backed debt and $650M of convertible notes.

takeaways.label: Profit goal slipping
takeaways.text: Opendoor admits it is behind its goal of positive adjusted net income by the end of 2026, blaming a slower market. Q3 adjusted net loss was $66M.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
